name: Hyderabad
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Hyderabad: pharma and life sciences diligence, IT vendor integrity, land title research and asset tracing.
hero_lede: Hyderabad, capital of Telangana, combines one of India's largest technology workforces with its leading cluster of bulk drug and life sciences manufacturing. TDSC helps clients research pharmaceutical and technology counterparties, test vendor and partner integrity, and check the land records behind the city's fast-growing real estate market.
intro: Hyderabad is the capital of Telangana and one of India's main technology and pharmaceutical centres. India Briefing reports that more than 900,000 people worked in IT and IT-enabled services across some 1,500 companies in 2023, with IT exports of about US$32 billion in FY 2022-23, second only to Bengaluru. Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Infosys and TCS run large operations in HITEC City, Madhapur and the Nanakramguda Financial District. The city is also called the bulk drug capital of India, producing about 40 percent of the country's bulk medicines, with Dr. Reddy's, Aurobindo, Bharat Biotech, Laurus Labs and multinational drug makers present and a 2,000-acre life sciences cluster at Genome Valley. Public sector defence and engineering firms such as BHEL, BEL and HAL also have long roots there.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Hyderabad because so much of the global pharmaceutical and technology supply chain runs through it. Buyers and licensors of active pharmaceutical ingredients, contract research and manufacturing services need confidence in their partners' ownership, quality record and regulatory history. Multinationals with large Hyderabad development centres face vendor kickbacks, conflicts of interest and departing staff who take data or clients. Rapid expansion of the western corridor around Kokapet, Gachibowli and the Financial District has made land a recurring subject of litigation and title disputes. Hyderabad founders, promoters and companies also feature in cross-border insolvency, fraud and enforcement matters.

matters.title: Pharmaceutical partner and API diligence
matters.text: Researching Hyderabad bulk drug, API and contract manufacturing companies before supply, licensing or acquisition deals: ownership and promoter history, related-party plants, regulatory inspection and recall history, litigation, and reputation among former staff and industry contacts, with findings set against public filings and regulator records.

matters.title: Development centre vendor integrity
matters.text: Checking staffing agencies, facilities, transport and IT subcontractors serving Hyderabad capability centres for undisclosed links to client employees, shared directors or addresses, shell entities and adverse records, where procurement kickbacks or inflated billing are suspected.

matters.title: Land title and corridor property
matters.text: Reviewing ownership chains, encumbrances, government land claims and pending litigation affecting plots and buildings in Kokapet, Gachibowli, Shamshabad and other growth areas, with local professionals obtaining lawfully available registration, revenue and court records before a lease, purchase or development commitment.

matters.title: Promoter and founder background research
matters.text: Building profiles of Hyderabad promoters, founders and senior executives ahead of investment or partnership, covering prior ventures, insolvency and tribunal proceedings, regulatory actions, political connections and media coverage in English and Telugu, and separating confirmed facts from reputation.

matters.title: Asset tracing for enforcement
matters.text: Identifying real estate, company interests, vehicles and business activity in Hyderabad and its suburbs linked to a judgment or award debtor, to support counsel seeking attachment, interim relief in aid of arbitration or recognition proceedings before the courts in Telangana.

local_context.title: Courts sitting in Hyderabad
local_context.text: The High Court for the State of Telangana sits in Hyderabad and exercises appellate and writ jurisdiction over the state. Commercial disputes of specified value are heard by commercial courts constituted under the Commercial Courts Act 2015, while other civil suits begin in the city civil courts. Hyderabad also hosts a bench of the National Company Law Tribunal for insolvency and company matters and a Debt Recovery Tribunal used by lenders.

local_context.title: IAMC Hyderabad and its land dispute
local_context.text: The International Arbitration and Mediation Centre, Hyderabad was set up in 2021 as an institutional venue for domestic and international arbitration. In June 2025 the Telangana High Court set aside the state's free allotment of land in Raidurg to the centre, and in February 2026 the Supreme Court dismissed IAMC's appeals. Reports indicate the High Court left in place the state's financial grant and its directive referring larger government disputes to IAMC.

local_context.title: Telangana land records
local_context.text: Agricultural land records in Telangana are maintained through a state online portal, and the Dharani system introduced in 2020 has been replaced under the Telangana Bhu Bharati legislation of 2025. Documents are registered through the state Registration and Stamps Department, and municipal property records sit with the city authorities. Changes to the land record system and disputes over government and assigned land make cross-checking against court records essential.

local_context.title: State industrial and investment framework
local_context.text: Telangana's TS-iPASS Act provides time-bound industrial clearances and what the state presents as a right to clearance; India Briefing reports 2,518 units sanctioned in FY 2022-23. State bodies such as TSIIC allot industrial land in parks and clusters. Allotment records, approvals and conditions attached to them can be directly relevant when testing a counterparty's claims about its facilities or permissions.

tdsc_approach: TDSC handles Hyderabad matters from Nashville and has no office in India. Engagements begin by identifying the records that bear on the question: Ministry of Corporate Affairs filings for the Telangana entities involved, orders of the Telangana High Court, commercial courts and the Hyderabad tribunals, regulatory and inspection records for pharmaceutical counterparties, and, for property, state land, registration and municipal records obtained lawfully. Telugu and Urdu-language press is reviewed where useful. Where enquiries on the ground are needed, such as site verification at a manufacturing unit or discreet industry interviews, TDSC coordinates experienced local professionals working with Indian counsel, without pretexting or access to bank, call or identity records. Findings separate documented fact from inference.

faqs.q: What should be checked before contracting with a Hyderabad API manufacturer?
faqs.a: Typically corporate ownership and promoter history, related plants and group companies, regulatory inspection outcomes and warning letters, product recalls, litigation and tribunal proceedings, and reputation among former staff and industry participants. We compare those findings with the company's own representations and identify what could not be confirmed, so quality and compliance teams can decide what to test further.

faqs.q: Is IAMC Hyderabad still a viable arbitration venue?
faqs.a: The centre continues to be referenced as an institution, but its free land allotment was set aside by the Telangana High Court in 2025, a decision the Supreme Court left standing in 2026. Forum selection is for counsel. TDSC supports arbitrations in Hyderabad or elsewhere with research on parties, witnesses and assets.

faqs.q: How reliable are Telangana land records for a Hyderabad property deal?
faqs.a: They are digitised but have been through significant change, with the Dharani portal replaced under 2025 legislation, and disputes over government, assigned and ceiling land are common around the city. We combine state land records, registration and encumbrance data, municipal records and court searches and highlight any inconsistency between them.

faqs.q: Which court hears a commercial dispute involving a Hyderabad company?
faqs.a: That depends on value and subject matter. Commercial disputes above the statutory threshold go to commercial courts under the Commercial Courts Act 2015, insolvency goes to the NCLT bench in Hyderabad, and writ petitions go to the Telangana High Court. Research for a dispute usually covers all three, since related proceedings often run in parallel.

faqs.q: Can TDSC investigate misconduct inside a Hyderabad development centre?
faqs.a: We support internal investigations led by the client and counsel by researching vendors, related parties and external links of the individuals involved through lawful sources. We do not access personal devices, accounts or call records. Device forensics and interviews are planned with counsel so that evidence is gathered consistently with India's data protection and employment rules.
